title: Ellzey's e-positivity conjecture for proper circular arc digraphs
statement:
Let $\vec G$ be a proper circular arc digraph: its vertices correspond to arcs on a circle whose left endpoints occur in clockwise order and which do not contain one another, with $(i,j)$ a directed edge exactly when the left endpoint of the $j$th arc lies in the $i$th arc. Let $X_{\vec G}(\bm x;q)$ be its chromatic quasisymmetric function, weighting proper colourings by $q^{\operatorname{asc}(\kappa)}$. The source states that this function is symmetric for such digraphs. It is **$e$-positive** if its expansion in the elementary basis has coefficients that are polynomials in $q$ with nonnegative coefficients.

**Ellzey's conjecture.** If $\vec G$ is a proper circular arc digraph, then $X_{\vec G}(\bm x;q)$ is $e$-positive.

This extends the refined Stanley–Stembridge conjecture from natural unit interval graphs to proper circular arc digraphs. The source states that this extension is open.
source_name: Foster Tom and Aarush Vailaya, “The chromatic symmetric function of graphs glued at a single vertex”, arXiv:2503.19344 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19344

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025). “This refined conjecture is still open.”
